def: A 14-digit code identifying your bank branch as an Authorised Dealer in foreign exchange. Registered on ICEGATE at each port so export proceeds and incentives can be credited.
The companion form to SPICe+ that applies for GSTIN, EPFO, ESIC, profession tax (Maharashtra, Karnataka, West Bengal), Shops & Establishment (some states) and a bank account during incorporation.

Under GST: all taxable, exempt, export and inter-state supplies of a PAN across India, excluding GST itself and inward reverse-charge supplies. Decides registration, composition, QRMP, e-invoicing and annual-return thresholds.
Articles of Association (internal rules) and Memorandum of Association (objects, capital, subscribers) of a company, filed electronically as e-AoA and e-MoA with SPICe+.
Income tax paid during the year in instalments (15 June, 15 September, 15 December, 15 March) when the year’s liability exceeds ₹10,000.
Former tax on share premium above fair market value received by closely held companies (section 56(2)(viib)). Abolished for issues from 1 April 2025.
Annual ROC filings: AOC-4 carries the audited financial statements (within 30 days of the AGM); MGT-7 is the annual return (MGT-7A for small companies and OPCs), due within 60 days of the AGM.
An edit log that accounting software must keep for every company from 1 April 2023, recording each change to the books with date and user.
Basic Customs Duty — the headline import duty on the CIF value of goods, set per 8-digit ITC-HS code in the Customs Tariff.
Bureau of Indian Standards. ISI mark for products under Quality Control Orders; Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) for electronics and IT goods; hallmarking for gold.
The customs declaration an importer (via a customs broker) files to clear imported goods and pay duty.
Chartered Accountant (audits, tax) and Company Secretary (company-law filings). Both sign filings you cannot sign yourself.
Customs House Agent (customs broker) licensed to file shipping bills and bills of entry on your behalf.
Incoterms. FOB: seller delivers goods on board at the origin port; CIF: seller also pays freight and insurance to the destination port. Indian customs values imports on CIF.
Corporate Identity Number of a company, LLP Identification Number, and Director Identification Number of an individual director/partner.

Simplified GST: pay a flat 1% (traders/manufacturers), 5% (restaurants) or 6% (services) of turnover, quarterly, without input credit or tax invoices. Turnover ceiling ₹1.5 crore (₹50 lakh for services).
Consent to Establish and Consent to Operate from the State Pollution Control Board, required for Green, Orange and Red category industries.
Directorate General of Foreign Trade — issues IEC, RCMC, authorisations and the Foreign Trade Policy.
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, with Rules notified 13 Nov 2025 and full obligations from 13 May 2027.
Free ‘startup’ status from the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade for entities under 10 years old with turnover below ₹200 crore working on innovation.
Digital Signature Certificate (Class 3) used to sign electronic filings on MCA, GST, DGFT and income-tax portals.
Electronic Bank Realisation Certificate — proof on DGFT’s portal that export proceeds were received; now self-certified by the exporter against bank IRMs.
A platform that owns, operates or manages a digital marketplace for others’ supplies. ECOs collect GST TCS (0.5%) and income-tax TDS (0.1%) from sellers.
A GST invoice registered on the Invoice Registration Portal, which returns an Invoice Reference Number and QR code. Mandatory above ₹5 crore aggregate turnover.
Electronic document required to move goods worth more than ₹50,000 (inter-state; many states for intra-state too).
Export Promotion Capital Goods scheme — import machinery at zero duty against an export obligation of six times the duty saved in six years.
Employees’ Provident Fund (20+ employees; 12% + 12%) and Employees’ State Insurance (10+ employees earning up to ₹21,000; 0.75% + 3.25%).
RBI filing within 30 days of allotting shares to a non-resident investor, made on the FIRMS portal.
Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 — governs every cross-border payment, foreign investment into India (FDI) and Indian investment abroad (ODI).
Foreign Inward Remittance Advice/Certificate from your bank or payment provider proving foreign money arrived with a purpose code.
Food Safety and Standards Authority of India. Every food business needs a registration or licence (FoSCoS portal) and a 14-digit number on labels.
15-character GST identification number: state code + PAN + entity code + checksum. One per state of registration.
Outward supplies statement (11th), summary return with payment (20th), annual return (31 Dec, above ₹2 crore) and reconciliation statement (above ₹5 crore).
Harmonised System of Nomenclature codes for goods and Services Accounting Codes for services, used to fix GST rates and on invoices.
Importer-Exporter Code, a 10-digit number (now same as PAN) from DGFT, mandatory for goods trade; ₹500; annual update April–June.
Integrated GST on inter-state and import supplies; Central and State GST split equally on intra-state supplies.
GST Invoice Management System — accept, reject or keep pending supplier invoices so your GSTR-2B input credit is accurate.
Declaration of commencement of business filed within 180 days of incorporation after subscribers pay for their shares.
GST you paid on purchases, offset against GST you collect on sales — available only if the supplier filed and the invoice shows in GSTR-2B.
India’s 8-digit version of the HS code used for customs tariff and import/export policy.
Limited Liability Partnership — a body corporate with partners whose liability is limited to their contribution; taxed at 30%.
Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 — label declarations (MRP, net quantity, manufacturer/importer, dates, country of origin) and registration for packers and importers.
Letter of Undertaking (Form RFD-11) filed yearly on the GST portal to export goods or services without paying IGST.
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises classified by investment and turnover (micro ≤ ₹2.5 cr / ₹10 cr). Udyam is the free registration portal.
National Industrial Classification 2008 code for your activity, needed in SPICe+, Udyam and many state forms.
National Single Window System — one login for DPIIT recognition and many central and state approvals.
Overseas Direct Investment — an Indian resident or company acquiring control or equity in a foreign entity; reported through an AD bank under the 2022 Overseas Investment Rules.
Online Information Database Access and Retrieval services — digital services supplied over the internet; foreign suppliers to Indian consumers must register and pay GST.
One Person Company — a private company with a single member and a nominee; converts to a normal private company at any time.
Permanent Account Number (tax identity) and Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number (for depositing TDS/TCS).
GST rule deciding which state’s tax applies — for goods, usually where delivery ends; for services, generally the recipient’s location.
Declaring income as a fixed percentage of turnover (6%/8% businesses up to ₹3 crore; 50% professionals up to ₹75 lakh) without books or audit. Section 58 of the Income-tax Act, 2025.
Quarterly Return, Monthly Payment scheme for GST taxpayers with turnover up to ₹5 crore.
Registration-Cum-Membership Certificate from an Export Promotion Council, needed for FTP benefits.
Reverse charge mechanism — the recipient (you) pays GST instead of the supplier, e.g., on imported services, legal services, and goods transport.
Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products — a refund of embedded taxes as transferable scrips, claimed via the shipping bill.
Registrar of Companies, the MCA office that receives company and LLP filings.
A non-profit company licensed under section 8 of the Companies Act; no dividends, eligible for 12A/80G.
The export customs declaration filed on ICEGATE; the document on which RoDTEP/drawback claims are made.
State law requiring registration of shops, offices and commercial establishments and governing hours, leave and holidays.
A private company with paid-up capital up to ₹10 crore and turnover up to ₹100 crore (from 1 Dec 2025) — lighter compliance.
RBI declaration for software exported in non-physical form, certified by STPI or a SEZ.
Simplified Proforma for Incorporating Company Electronically Plus — the MCA web form that reserves the name (Part A) and incorporates (Part B).
Annual audit of a company’s accounts by a Chartered Accountant under the Companies Act — mandatory for every company regardless of size.
Audit under section 63 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (old 44AB) above ₹1 crore turnover (₹10 crore if ≤5% cash) or ₹50 lakh professional receipts; report due 30 September.
The 2025 Act’s single 12-month period (1 April–31 March) replacing ‘previous year’ and ‘assessment year’.
Tax collected at source (by sellers/platforms) and tax deducted at source (by payers) — advance tax credits that appear in Form 26AS/AIS and the GST cash ledger.
Trade Receivables Discounting System — platforms (RXIL, M1xchange, Invoicemart) where MSMEs discount invoices on large buyers.
Unique Identification Number the RBI assigns to each overseas investment, quoted in all later remittances and APRs.
Exports and supplies to SEZs: taxed at 0% while input credit remains refundable.
